intro: Same prompt, four AIs, and us. Entertainment only. Graded at the DraftKings line each side was asked.
prompt_note: PROVISIONAL BOARD: asked Wednesday Nov 11, 2026 (prompt sent about 1:55 to 2:25 PM PT) on the DraftKings line fetched at 1:30 PM PT, before the Westgate SuperContest card was out. This is not a Westgate run. NE vs DET is in Munich (neutral). Byes: CHI, DEN, PHI, TB. Each AI got the identical prompt and picked all 14 games with a 1-10 confidence, three Best Bets and a ranked top 5. Grok's first attempt returned an error and was rerun in a new chat at 2:29 PM PT. Grok's chosen side runs against its own stated number in most games; its picks are shown exactly as given. Vector's sides are leans from a provisional model update (injury layer not fully re-reconciled); its top 5 is provisional and it has no Best Bets until the Westgate card posts. All 14 games are pending.
line_source: DraftKings line, Wednesday Nov 11, 2026 (fetched 1:30 PM PT)
score_source: ESPN NFL scoreboard (https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/nfl/scoreboard?week=10&seasontype=2&dates=2026). Only games with status final are stored. No Week 10 finals stored yet.

WAS@NYG.reason: Washington is missing its top WR, left tackle and both starting DTs. The Giants' record is soft, so this is about Washington

NE@DET.reason: Even ratings on a neutral field. New England has faced the 3rd-hardest slate, Detroit the 23rd

KC@ATL.reason: Kansas City's margin came against the 29th-ranked slate and Mahomes has a sore throwing elbow. I get the hook above 3

BUF@NYJ.reason: Four of Buffalo's seven wins came by 8 or fewer, and this is a road game six days after Monday night

CAR@NO.reason: Coin flip. My final number sits 0.2 from the line

HOU@CLE.reason: Adjusted margins put these teams 2.5 apart on a neutral field. Caution: all five Cleveland wins were by 4 or fewer

MIN@GB.reason: Ratings are close and Green Bay is thin at running back and linebacker. Minnesota's unsettled QB keeps this low

MIA@IND.reason: Coin flip between two depleted teams. A first-time starter against a club that traded two of its best linemen

JAX@TEN.reason: Jacksonville is my No. 1, but five of Tennessee's seven losses were by 7 or fewer and the Titans come off a bye

LAR@ARI.reason: The Rams rank 15th here and are likely without Nacua and Adams. Risk: Beck's debut against a strong pass rush

SEA@LV.reason: Seattle leans on a hurt backup QB with its left tackle doubtful. Risk: Mendoza's debut

SF@DAL.reason: Near coin flip. Home field and San Francisco's thin WR group account for a half-point edge

PIT@CIN.reason: Coin flip. Cincinnati is 2nd in adjusted margin, but Pittsburgh is rested and won the first meeting 30-27

LAC@BAL.reason: The Chargers are 0-8 with the league's worst adjusted margin, a patched line and no Derwin James. Brissett's debut caps it

WAS@NYG.reason: Giants defense at home covers the short number against a battered Commanders squad.

NE@DET.reason: Neutral site favors the better overall roster; Detroit's offense outpaces NE.

KC@ATL.reason: KC is elite and only laying a field goal and a hook against a flailing Falcons team.

BUF@NYJ.reason: Buffalo is blowing teams out; the Jets offense cannot keep pace.

CAR@NO.reason: Coin flip divisional game; giving a slight mathematical edge to home field.

MIA@IND.reason: Getting the hook over a field goal makes Miami the mathematical side in an ugly game.

JAX@TEN.reason: Double-digit divisional home dogs are historically a strong systemic play.

LAR@ARI.reason: LAR missing Nacua and market is inflated; Arizona getting nearly 10 at home is value.

SEA@LV.reason: Fading the large road favorite against a rookie QB who brings unknown upside.

SF@DAL.reason: San Francisco is dominant; Dallas defense cannot stop them.

PIT@CIN.reason: Divisional prime-time game; taking the points with Pittsburgh's elite defense.

LAC@BAL.reason: Ravens missing Lamar, but Chargers are winless; swallowing the points.

WAS@NYG.reason: I make New York roughly a four-point favorite after the blend. The Giants have the better record, and Washington loses center Lucas Patrick.

NE@DET.reason: This game is almost exactly on the number. Detroit has the better point differential, but its schedule has been considerably easier.

KC@ATL.reason: Kansas City has a considerably better underlying profile. Atlanta is 3-6 and has a negative 35-point differential.

BUF@NYJ.reason: Buffalo has a 7-1 record, +69 differential and a difficult schedule. The Jets are 2-7 and have a -41 differential.

CAR@NO.reason: My fair number actually makes Carolina a tiny favorite. New Orleans gets two home-field points, bringing the blended number to Saints -1.6.

HOU@CLE.reason: Houston has the better point differential despite the losing record. However, Cleveland is at home, and my independent number is Houston by only about 3.3.

MIN@GB.reason: Green Bay loses Josh Jacobs, which matters to its offensive balance. Minnesota's quarterback situation is significantly unsettled.

MIA@IND.reason: Miami is 1-7 and has lost Malik Willis to injured reserve. Kyle McCord is in line for his first NFL start.

JAX@TEN.reason: Jacksonville is 6-2 with a +108 point differential. Tennessee is 1-7 with a -55 differential.

LAR@ARI.reason: The Rams are the better team, but the market asks them to win by almost 10. Puka Nacua's absence matters, while Arizona has named rookie Carson Beck as its starter after Gardner Minshew's injury.

SEA@LV.reason: This is one of my more interesting underdog positions. Sam Darnold is ruled out, and Drew Lock is expected to start.

SF@DAL.reason: San Francisco is 7-1 and has the league's best point differential among these teams at +79. The 49ers' played schedule has been relatively soft, which prevents me from making the margin excessively large.

PIT@CIN.reason: Cincinnati has a +65 point differential and is 6-2. The Bengals have also been producing explosive offensive performances.

LAC@BAL.reason: Baltimore's quarterback situation is the biggest factor. Lamar Jackson is out, with Jacoby Brissett expected to start.
